section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the analytic strategy for a single daily-diary study using multilevel modeling to separate within-person (daily) and between-person (weekly) variance; predictors were disaggregated into person means and daily deviations and centered. Four multilevel models were run (for intuitive eating, body appreciation, body image concerns, and negative affect) with BMI as a covariate, and interactions between daily/weekly self-compassion and daily/weekly frequency of interactions with body-focused others were tested and probed with simple slopes.
section_summary.evidence_source: Multilevel modeling is the ideal data analytic approach when examining hierarchical data structures, such as those from daily diary studies in which assessment days are nested within participants. Four multilevel models were run in SAS 9.3 with raw scores on intuitive eating, body appreciation, body image concerns, and negative affect across study days serving as the criteria variables.
